title: Finitely generated ideal defining support of finitely presented module
statement: Let B be a commutative ring and M a finitely presented B-module. There exists a finitely generated ideal I of B such that Module.support B M = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus I.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation B^u → B^v → M → 0 and let I be generated by the finitely many maximal minors of its presentation matrix.

For each prime p, the localization M_p vanishes exactly when I is not contained in p: one implication multiplies annihilators of the finite generators and applies Cauchy–Binet; the converse uses a maximal minor outside p and the adjugate identity.
The set of maximal minors is finite, so its span I is finitely generated, and the preceding equivalence is exactly support = zeroLocus I.
